subject: Data derivatives, residency constraints & subprocessor routing
messages:
From: Amelia Ross <amelia@healthsuite.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@healthsuite.ai>
Date: 2026-08-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify data derivatives & subprocessor routing for pilot

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. Before we sign the pilot DPA I need a couple of clarifications from your side so our legal team can sign off quickly:

1) Derivative outputs: Can you confirm whether Redwood will assert any rights over model responses generated from our tenant data during the pilot? HealthSuite requires that generated responses and any derivative artifacts be exclusively ours or at least not claimed by the vendor.

2) No-training commitment: We see language in the draft about not using customer data for model improvement without consent. For the pilot can you provide operational evidence (where the data is stored/processed, and whether any telemetry is used for model updates)?

3) Subprocessors & residency: We need the current ingress/egress subprocessor list and whether any subprocessors are in-scope for storing prompts/responses outside the US. If there are transfers, we need an export/control plan.

I've attached the DPA redlines our counsel proposed (HealthSuite-DPA-redlines.docx) and a short questionnaire they asked us to fill if you prefer.

Appreciate a short summary and a contact from Redwood legal/ops who can provide the evidence pack. We are targeting a Sep 1 start for the pilot.

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Ross
Head of Platform Partnerships
HealthSuite.ai

-- attachment: HealthSuite-DPA-redlines.docx (docx) --
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia@healthsuite.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify data derivatives & subprocessor routing for pilot

Amelia, thanks — quick answers and a plan below. I'm looping in Ben (sales) and Lauren (legal ops) to provide the evidence pack.

Quick summary (high level):
- Derivative outputs: Redwood does not claim ownership of tenant outputs. Customers retain rights to prompts and responses produced by the model when the data is provided as part of a tenant workload. We are happy to include a clear clause in the DPA and the SOW that states that outputs remain customer property for your pilot.

- No-training commitment: For the hosted pilot we will enforce a no-training flag for your tenant which prevents use of prompt/response data in any model training pipelines or improvement datasets. Operationally: requests for the pilot are routed to a dedicated tenancy with KV cache isolation; we will not export logs to training buckets. Lauren will share an evidence snapshot showing the tenancy and log retention settings.

- Subprocessors & residency: The current infra subprocessors that may touch prompt/responses are listed in our inventory (I attached the most recent CSV). All production storage for your pilot can be restricted to US regions; any cross-border transfers are handled per the DPA and require explicit routing policies.

Next steps I propose:
1) Lauren to send the subprocessor inventory + short evidence pack (on tenancy, retention, and no-train toggle) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Ben to confirm commercial start date and whether the Sep 1 pilot start is firm.
3) I can provide a short one-page language artifact to insert into section 4 (data use) of your redlines so counsel can move quickly.

For transparency I'm attaching our working redlines file (HealthSuite-DPA-redlines.docx) and the subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_inventory.csv).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
-- attachment: subprocessor_inventory.csv (csv) --

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify data derivatives & subprocessor routing for pilot

Karthik / Ben — I've pulled the evidence items we usually share for pilot DPAs; below is what I'll produce and where I'm short and need input:

Items to deliver (target EOD 8/26):
- Subprocessor inventory (latest): CSV attached. It includes service role, region, and whether it stores telemetry. If HealthSuite needs US-only residency we can mark their tenant for US-only storage.
- No-train confirmation: signed operational runbook + screenshot of the tenancy flag that disables model-improvement pipelines for a tenant.
- Dataflow diagram: high-level PDF showing request routing, KV cache isolation, and any transient buffers.
- Retention & export controls: retention settings and steps for producing a proof-of-deletion if needed.

Open question for Ben/Karthik: can we commit to providing SFTP export of tenant logs to HealthSuite for the pilot (48h SLA) if they request an audit? That will satisfy their counsel faster but is slightly manual for us.

I'll attach the inventory and the runbook snapshot once I finish.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Lauren / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and attachments. Counsel reviewed Lauren's notes and the inventory; two quick confirmations before we sign:

1) Confirm in writing that Redwood will add the explicit "no-claim on outputs" sentence to section 4 and that the no-train flag will be active for the pilot period. That language should be sufficient for our GC.

2) For the SFTP/audit option: yes, we would like the SFTP export of tenant logs as an audit artifact if you can commit to a 48h turnaround on requests for the pilot. Please confirm.

If you can send the updated DPA with the added language and confirm the SFTP turnaround I'll route to our GC for signature. We remain on-track for a Sep 1 pilot start pending contract.

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Ross
Head of Platform Partnerships
HealthSuite.ai
